{{Short description|British mathematician and academic}}
'''Jenefer Golding''' is a [[British people|British]] mathematician.  She is a professor of mathematics policy and practice at the [[University College London]] [[UCL Institute of Education|Institute of Education]]. 

Golding graduated from [[St Hugh's College, Oxford]] in 1971 with a degree in mathematics. After spending several years teaching schoolchildren, she moved to [[University College London|UCL]], where she focuses on development of mathematics education policy.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.maths.ox.ac.uk/about-us/engagement/alumni-stories/jennie-golding|title=Jennie Golding|publisher=[[Mathematical Institute, University of Oxford|University of Oxford Mathematical Institute]]|accessdate=29 March 2026}}</ref>

In 2016, she served as president of the [[Mathematical Association]], a [[Professional association|professional association]] which is involved in issues of [[Mathematics education|mathematics education]] in the UK.<ref>{{cite web|author = <!-- not stated --> |title = Jenefer (Jennie) Golding |url = https://profiles.ucl.ac.uk/48425-jenefer-jennie-golding |website = University College London profiles |location = London |publisher = University College London |access-date = 29 March 2026}}</ref>

In January 2024, she submitted written testimony to the [[Education Select Committee]] of the [[Parliament of the United Kingdom|UK Parliament]] which was published as part of the report called ''Delivering effective financial education'' in May of 2024.<ref>{{Citation |year=2024 |title=Delivering effective financial education |publisher=House of Commons Education Committee |url=https://committees.parliament.uk/publications/44814/documents/222577/default/ |access-date=29 March 2026}}</ref>
